R3 reads these frozen artifacts and does not rewrite R2 or claim that the failed R2 gate passed.

The safetensors bundle was parsed independently from its binary header and payload without torch, safetensors or the executor scorer. It is 298,304 bytes with a 3,384-byte header, schema slx08-context-vectors-r2 and exactly 36 unique expected keys for 12 unique cells times dense/corrected/legacy. Every tensor is little-endian float32 with shape [8, 1, 256], all offsets are contiguous and cover the complete 294,912-byte data region, all 73,728 scalar values are finite, and all 36 tensor-byte SHA-256 values match the frozen R2 samples.

An independent fixed-order implementation using struct-decoded row-major float32 values, math.fsum for dot products and squared norms, and math.sqrt reproduced all 24 canonical cosines exactly. The selected-block median is 0.9954494256753561 and the legacy median is 0.9918341527542236. Maximum absolute difference from the executor payload is 0.0 for both arms. Corrected exceeds legacy in 12/12 retained cells, while 10/12 corrected cells individually exceed 0.95; only the preregistered population median is an acceptance metric.

The frozen scorer was invoked twice through two sequential subprocess.run calls in separate WSL processes, with distinct output targets and logs. canonical_evaluation.json and repeat_evaluation.json are exactly equal and each has canonical payload SHA-256 b6f3124c0baed6ced6942a81c9eda0f1d8e7dcb46682c8059ce909dc73d51ff0. The R3 samples JSONL is an exact row-for-row projection of that payload. This repetition proves determinism of one frozen implementation, not independent scientific replication; the separate binary-parser recomputation in this review supplies the implementation-independent check.

The canonical scorer removes the invalid CUDA-versus-CPU scalar equality comparison from the successor contract without relaxing the original fidelity threshold of 0.95. No tolerance is fitted to the observed discrepancies and the raw float32 tensor identities remain exact. This supports the bounded diagnosis that R2 was a comparator false negative, but does not retroactively change R2's rejection.

R3 is intentionally a post-R2 retained-evidence rescore: the 12-cell population and its favorable median were already observed when the successor was designed. That double use would invalidate a claim of new prospective validation, generalization or a fresh efficacy estimate. It does not invalidate the allowed comparator-diagnosis claim because R3 introduces no new sample and freezes only a deterministic, auditable reduction over the complete retained population. The 0.95 result must be reported as a reproducibility property of R2 evidence, not new evidence of model quality or runtime behavior.
